comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and composition of Commercial Real Estate loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Commercial real estate loans consist of originated and purchased loans directly or indirectly secured by hotels, retail stores, multifamily housing complexes, and commercial/industrial properties, as well as loans to clients warehousing assets backed by commercial real estate.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose specific data and definitions related to Commercial Real Estate (CRE) loans. BAC quantifies its 2023 CRE outstandings at $66.8 billion for U.S. and $6.1 billion for non-U.S. exposures. GS defines its CRE loans as including originated and purchased loans secured by hotels, retail stores, multifamily housing, and commercial/industrial properties, as well as warehoused assets. While BAC provides aggregate outstanding balances, GS provides the structural definition of what constitutes a CRE loan in its portfolio.

sentences.text: (4)Total outstandings includes U.S. commercial real estate loans of $66.8 billion and non-U.S. commercial real estate loans of $6.1 billion.

• Commercial Real Estate. Commercial real estate loans includes originated loans that are directly or indirectly secured by hotels, retail stores, multifamily housing complexes and commercial and industrial properties. Commercial real estate loans also includes loans extended to clients who warehouse assets that are directly or indirectly backed by commercial real estate. In addition, commercial real estate includes loans purchased by the firm.
